_note: Batch 8 — single-family rentals (institutional 'Wall Street landlord' operators). Imported via import-to-airtable.mjs; businesses land review_status=pending, evidence lands publish=true but still needs the publish checkbox verified. Scope: PE-owned landlords only. DR Horton and other homebuilders are publicly traded and excluded (relevant only as builders that sell build-to-rent communities in bulk to these landlords). Blackstone appears twice: Invitation Homes (ownership_status=former — Blackstone created it in 2012 and exited by ~2019, now NYSE:INVH) and Tricon Residential (confirmed — Blackstone took it private in 2024). Tier A evidence: FTC $48M settlement vs Invitation Homes (2024). Blackstone already exists as a firm (Batch 5) with no firm tags, so its two SFR businesses inherit nothing. NOT attached: the 2022 House Financial Services Committee report on institutional landlords (industry-level, names multiple firms — no single-firm home).

firms.notes: Founded and owns Progress Residential, the largest US institutional single-family landlord. Led by former Goldman Sachs executive Don Mullen.
Owner of FirstKey Homes, one of the largest US single-family rental platforms.
Runs the Main Street Renewal single-family rental platform; manages roughly $20B.

businesses.platform_company: The largest US single-family landlord; created by Blackstone in 2012 after the foreclosure crisis, taken public in 2017, and fully exited by Blackstone by ~2019 (now NYSE: INVH)

evidence.description: FTC settlement ($48M, Sept 2024): the FTC charged Invitation Homes with deceiving renters on price, charging undisclosed 'junk fees' (mandatory monthly charges for smart-home tech and air-filter delivery costing up to ~$1,700/yr), withholding security deposits (returned in only ~40% of cases vs. a ~64% norm), and unfair eviction practices — including steering pandemic-era renters away from the CDC declaration that would have protected them from eviction. Invitation paid $48M in consumer refunds (no admission of wrongdoing). Blackstone founded and ran the company 2012–2019; the FTC's conduct period spans 2018–2023.

businesses.platform_company: Largest US institutional single-family landlord (~94,000 homes as of 2025), including scattered-site and build-to-rent

evidence.description: Progress charges an array of fees on top of rent (e.g., a $200 eviction-administration fee, a $75 maintenance-visit fee, per-pet fees, and a 10% late fee) and has been an aggressive evictor, filing on tenants only a single month behind. Congress investigated whether Progress and peers filed evictions during the pandemic moratorium, and Sen. Sherrod Brown questioned why its pandemic-era eviction filings fell disproportionately on majority-Black communities. Tenants formed a 3,000+ member 'Victims of Progress Residential' group citing lost deposits, fees, and unaddressed maintenance.

businesses.platform_company: ~40,000 US homes; Blackstone took Tricon private in May 2024 for ~$3.5B — its return to single-family rentals and now its primary US SFR platform (it also absorbed the wound-down Home Partners of America)
One of the largest US single-family rental platforms, owned by Cerberus Capital Management
Amherst's single-family rental platform — roughly 16,000 homes across the Midwest and Sunbelt
